review: The printed grid is 5/4/4/4 and the Arabic prints the closing line of stanzas 2–4 in parentheses — as an aside rather than a rhyme line. The payload keeps those as regular lines (the corpus stores them as the fourth line) but the review records that they are parenthetical in the print.

1:3–1:4 מִי־לִי בַשָּׁמַיִם … וּמִי עִמְּךָ אֶחְפֹּץ בָּאָרֶץ — Psalm 73:25 almost verbatim (מִי־לִי בַשָּׁמָיִם וְעִמְּךָ לֹא־חָפַצְתִּי בָאָרֶץ); the Arabic مَنْ لِي سِوَاكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ أَرْتَجِي … is that verse, and the Hebrew keeps the fronted 'who' of each half.

1:1 and 1:5 both open with מַה־מָּתוֹק and the first word of the Arabic (كَمْ أَنْتَ حُلْوٌ / حُلْوٌ حُلْوٌ) is 'sweet' threefold in 1:5; the Hebrew keeps the threefold מָתוֹק in 1:5, because the stanza builds to that acclamation.

3:1–3:2 the Arabic فِي الضِّيقِ … فِي شِدَّةِ الْآلَامِ is 'in straits … in the grip of pains'; the Hebrew keeps עֶזְרָתִי וְנִצְחוֹנִי as the pair of Ps 121:2 and the passive sense of 'able in You' rather than a bare 'You were able'.

4:1–4:2 הוֹדַעְתַּנִי אַהֲבָתְךָ … הִכְלַמְתַּנִי — the Arabic عَرَّفْتَنِي حُبَّكَ … أَخْجَلْتَنِي pairs a revelation with a shaming-for-short-love; the Hebrew keeps the causative verbs with the suffixed object, so the Lord's love remains the agent even in the rebuke.
2:2 חֶבְרָתִי עִם־אִישׁוּתְךָ — 'my company with Your person'; אִישׁוּת is the glossary noun used in hymns 165 and 182, kept so the delight is specifically in the person.
